subtopic: The Argand Plane and Polar Representation
title: The Argand plane: distance and direction

board_content.text: Complex numbers as points and arrows
$z=x+iy$ is the point $(x,y)$, or the arrow from the origin to it.
The horizontal axis is real, the vertical axis is imaginary.

board_content.caption: Modulus is the length; argument is the angle

board_content.text: Modulus $|z|=r$ is how far (distance); argument $\arg z=\theta$ is which way (bearing).
Same point, two descriptions: Cartesian '$x$ east, $y$ north' or polar '$r$ at angle $\theta$'.
Multiplying by $i$ ($r=1$, $\theta=90^{\circ}$) is a pure quarter-turn.

segments_english.text: <curious>So far complex numbers were algebra. Now let's see them.</curious> On the Argand plane they become points and arrows.
z equals x plus i y is simply the point with coordinates x comma y, or equivalently the arrow from the origin out to that point.
The horizontal axis carries the real part, and the vertical axis carries the imaginary part. That's the whole picture.
Think of flying a kite from a rooftop. Two numbers fix the kite: the length of string, and the angle the string makes with the horizon.
Those two numbers are exactly the modulus and the argument. The modulus r tells you how far the point is; the argument theta tells you which direction, like a compass bearing.
The two pictures connect through simple trigonometry: x equals r cosine theta, and y equals r sine theta.

So it's one point with two descriptions. Cartesian says go x east and y north. Polar says go distance r at angle theta. An auto-rickshaw direction and a straight-line bearing for the same destination.
And here's the payoff coming: multiplying by i, which has modulus one and angle ninety degrees, is a pure quarter-turn, exactly the rotation picture from the first subtopic, now made precise.

segments_hinglish.text: <curious>Ab tak complex numbers algebra the. Ab inhe dekhte hain.</curious> Argand plane par ye points aur arrows ban jaate hain.
z equals x plus i y bas wo point hai jiske coordinates hain x comma y, ya equivalently origin se us point tak jaata arrow.
Horizontal axis real part rakhti hai, aur vertical axis imaginary part. Bas yehi poori picture hai.
Socho chhat se patang uda rahe ho. Do numbers patang ko fix karte hain: dhaage ki length, aur dhaaga horizon se jo angle banata hai.
Wo do numbers bilkul modulus aur argument hain. Modulus r batata hai point kitna door hai; argument theta batata hai kaunsi direction, jaise compass bearing.
Dono pictures simple trigonometry se judti hain: x equals r cosine theta, aur y equals r sine theta.
To ek hi point, do descriptions. Cartesian kehta hai x east aur y north jao. Polar kehta hai distance r, angle theta par jao. Ek hi destination ke liye do raaste bataana.
Aur ye raha aane wala payoff: i se multiply karna, jiska modulus one aur angle ninety degrees hai, ek pure quarter-turn hai, bilkul pehle subtopic wali rotation picture, ab precise.
